2609.00808.title: Ctrl-F-Resist. Practices, Challenges, and Technical Needs of Civil Society Organizations Monitoring the Far-Right Online
2609.00808.paper_summary: As far-right actors increasingly exploit online platforms to disseminate ideology and mobilize supporters, civil society organizations (CSOs) play a vital yet underrecognized role in monitoring antidemocratic dynamics online. Unlike fact-checkers or content moderators, CSOs engage in long-term, contextualized analysis, often in resource-constrained settings and under precarious conditions. Despite their critical societal role, CSOs face significant barriers to adopting or co-developing technical solutions, including legal uncertainty, limited platform access, and chronic underfunding. Existing research and tool development efforts have largely overlooked these actors in favor of more institutionally embedded stakeholders. This paper addresses this gap through a qualitative study with 15 practitioners from 12 Germany-based CSOs engaged in online monitoring, positioning them as key yet overlooked stakeholders in the governance of digital spaces. We explore their current practices, challenges, and expectations regarding technological support. Our findings show that monitoring remains largely manual due to the lack of tailored tools, with enhanced search capabilities emerging as the most pressing technical need. While participants express openness to AI-supported features such as media processing and content discovery, many remain skeptical of automated classification, citing concerns around trust, legal usability, and professional credibility. Grounded in these findings, we introduce a conceptual monitoring workflow and describe its implementation in an open-source Telegram monitoring prototype designed to flexibly support diverse monitoring goals. We outline concrete design, policy, and research recommendatios, and introduce the manual labor trap as an empirically grounded concept that explains why monitoring CSOs tend to remain locked into labor-intensive, low-capacity arrangements.
2609.00808.paper_summary_zh: 隨著極右派行動者越來越多地利用線上平台來傳播意識形態和動員支持者，公民社會組織（CSOs）在監測線上反民主動態方面扮演著重要但未被充分認識的角色。與事實查核者或內容審核者不同，CSOs 進行長期且具情境性的分析，通常在資源有限和條件不穩定的環境中進行。儘管他們在社會中扮演著關鍵角色，CSOs 在採用或共同開發技術解決方案時面臨重大障礙，包括法律不確定性、有限的平台訪問和持續的資金不足。現有的研究和工具開發工作在很大程度上忽視了這些行動者，而更偏向於那些制度嵌入性更強的利益相關者。本文通過對 12 家位於德國的 CSOs 的 15 位從業者進行的定性研究來填補這一空白，將他們定位為數位空間治理中關鍵但被忽視的利益相關者。我們探討了他們目前的實踐、挑戰和對技術支持的期望。我們的研究結果顯示，由於缺乏量身定制的工具，監測仍然主要是手動進行，增強的搜索能力成為最迫切的技術需求。雖然參與者對於 AI 支持的功能，如媒體處理和內容發現表示開放，但許多人對自動分類持懷疑態度，並指出對信任、法律可用性和專業可信度的擔憂。在這些發現的基礎上，我們介紹了一個概念性的監測工作流程，並描述其在一個開源的 Telegram 監測原型中的實施，該原型旨在靈活支持多樣的監測目標。我們概述了具體的設計、政策和研究建議，並引入了手動勞動陷阱作為一個基於實證的概念，解釋為何監測 CSOs 往往會陷入勞動密集型、低能力的安排中。
2609.00808.author: Elisabeth Steffen et.al.
